source_document: Manulife FlexCare SAMPLE policy (32 pages), as indexed in app/demo_index
description: Evaluation set v2. Supersedes notebooks/eval/eval_questions.json (v1) once the harness switches over in M1b; every v1 question is carried over and keeps its v1 id in `v1_id`. Ground truth was drafted from the demo index text and reviewed by the project owner. Evidence phrases are checked against the index by tests/test_eval_set.py.

behaviors.answer: Answer from the policy and cite a passage on one of expected_pages.
behaviors.defer: The policy defers the specific amount or detail to the Schedule of Benefits (not part of this document). A correct answer says so and cites the deferring passage; 'I don't know' is wrong.
behaviors.abstain: The policy does not cover the question. The system must reply exactly "I don't know".

categories.direct_fact: One fact stated plainly in the policy.
categories.paraphrase: Everyday wording that differs from the policy's terms.
categories.numeric: The answer is a specific amount, duration or age.
categories.multi_part: Two or more facts in one question, usually from one section.
categories.multi_chunk: The answer needs passages from different pages or sections.
categories.deferred: The policy points to the Schedule of Benefits instead of stating the amount.
categories.near_miss_oos: Insurance-related, but not covered anywhere in this policy.
categories.clear_oos: Unrelated to insurance or the policy.
categories.adversarial: Prompt injection, false premises, or requests for advice/actions the assistant must not give.

items.question: Is physiotherapy covered under paramedical services?
items.reference_answer: Yes. Paramedical services cover licensed and registered practitioners including physiotherapy, up to the difference between what the government health insurance plan covers and reasonable and customary charges. A physician or nurse practitioner referral may be required for the first visit.

evidence.text: naturopath, chiropodist, podiatrist, physiotherapy, massage therapist, and dietitian

items.question: When is a Prior Authorization form needed?
items.reference_answer: Before purchasing any product or service over $300, and before buying or arranging items such as oxygen, a standard non-electric wheelchair, a hospital adjustable bed, homecare or nursing, hearing aids, prosthetic appliances, orthotics, medical equipment and supplies, and accidental dental. The form must be signed by a medical professional.

evidence.text: Before purchasing any product or service exceeding $300, you must send us a Prior Authorization form

items.question: What expenses are excluded from health care benefits?
items.reference_answer: Among others: expenses payable under a government plan or manufacturer rebate program; cosmetic care (except reconstructive surgery); services that aren't medically necessary or are experimental; pandemic screening tests; charges above usual, reasonable and customary; war and terrorism; self-prescribed items or items prescribed by family members; and items not approved by Health Canada.

evidence.text: care, services or supplies for cosmetic purposes, except when in connection with reconstructive surgery

items.question: Who is eligible for coverage under this policy?
items.reference_answer: You must be a resident of Canada, have coverage under your government health insurance plan, be at least 18 on the application date (except children of an insured person), and Quebec residents must also be registered under the RAMQ drug plan or equivalent group coverage.

evidence.text: be at least 18 years of age on the date of application for this policy

items.question: Are emergency medical travel benefits covered under this policy?
items.reference_answer: Yes. Emergency medical travel benefits are automatically included for insured people under age 70 and cover eligible emergency expenses outside your home province or territory, above what the government plan pays, up to $5 million per insured person per incident.

evidence.text: this plan provides up to $5 million in total benefits per insured person

items.question: Is dental coverage included, and on which plans?
items.reference_answer: The dental benefit is available except on the DrugPlus and HealthStarter plans; coverage amounts are in the Schedule of Benefits.

evidence.text: Dental benefit (not available on DrugPlus or HealthStarter plans)

items.notes: Page 2 (table of contents) states the same restriction, so citing it is also correct.

items.question: What is the conversion privilege when a dependent's coverage ends?
items.reference_answer: When a dependent's coverage ends (for example on reaching age 21, marriage, becoming an orphan or getting employment), they can continue coverage under their own separate policy if they contact Manulife within 30 days of their coverage ending.

evidence.text: the insured must contact us within 30 days of their coverage ending

items.question: Can I name a beneficiary under this policy?
items.reference_answer: No. There is no right to name a beneficiary under this policy.

evidence.text: There is no right to name a beneficiary under this policy

items.question: Is laser eye surgery covered under the vision benefit?
items.reference_answer: Yes. When prescribed by a registered, certified or licensed ophthalmologist or optometrist, laser eye surgery is covered up to the maximum in the Schedule of Benefits.

evidence.text: laser eye surgery

items.question: Are paramedical services provided by a family member covered?
items.reference_answer: No. Paramedical services provided by a family member are excluded, and in general the service provider may not be an immediate family member.

evidence.text: services provided by a family member

items.question: Do I need approval before buying a wheelchair?
items.reference_answer: Yes. You must send a Prior Authorization form signed by a medical professional before buying a standard non-electric wheelchair (and before any equipment purchase over $300).

evidence.text: standard non- electric wheelchair

items.question: Will the plan pay for my massage therapy?
items.reference_answer: Yes, massage therapy by a licensed and registered massage therapist is covered under paramedical services, up to the difference between the government plan amount and reasonable and customary charges.

evidence.text: massage therapist

items.question: Can I get my money back if I cancel within the first month?
items.reference_answer: Yes. During the 30-day free-look period you can cancel and receive a full refund, minus the Vitality charge and any claims paid.

evidence.text: The first 30 days of your policy are known as the free- look period

items.question: Does the plan help pay for seeing a therapist for stress?
items.reference_answer: Yes. The mental health and therapy benefit covers direct counselling by a registered psychologist, clinical counsellor, registered psychotherapist, registered marriage and family therapist or registered social worker, including for stress management and emotional problems.

evidence.text: registered social worker for stress management, emotional problems

items.question: If I miss a premium payment, do I lose my coverage right away?
items.reference_answer: No. You have a 31-day grace period to pay the overdue amount; coverage ends on the last day of the grace period if payment isn't received.

evidence.text: you have a 31 -day grace period to pay the overdue amount

items.question: Are my kids still covered once they turn 21?
items.reference_answer: No. An insured child must be removed from the policy when they turn 21, but they can convert to their own policy if Manulife is contacted within 30 days of the coverage ending.

evidence.text: an insured child turns 21, gets married, becomes an orphan, or obtains full -time employment

items.question: Does it cover the ambulance ride to the hospital?
items.reference_answer: Yes. Medically necessary professional ground and air emergency ambulance transportation to a hospital within your home province or territory is covered (the difference between the government allowance and reasonable charges), with no lifetime maximum. Private ambulances and trips from a hospital to a residence are not covered.

evidence.text: ground and air emergency ambulance transportation within your home province or territo ry to a hospital

items.question: Will they pay for my glasses?
items.reference_answer: Yes. Prescription eyeglasses (lenses and frames) and contact lenses are covered up to the maximum in the Schedule of Benefits when prescribed by an ophthalmologist or optometrist. Safety glasses and non-prescription sunglasses are not covered.

evidence.text: prescription eyeglasses, including lenses and frames

items.question: How long is the grace period for overdue premiums?
items.reference_answer: 31 days.

evidence.text: 31 -day grace period

items.question: Within what time period must a claim have happened for it to be paid?
items.reference_answer: Within the last 12 months.

evidence.text: happened within the last 12 months

items.question: What is the maximum for accidental dental under emergency medical travel benefits?
items.reference_answer: $2,000, including all related treatment costs.

evidence.text: up to a maximum of $2,000

items.question: What fee is charged if a premium payment is returned for insufficient funds?
items.reference_answer: A $25 administration fee.

evidence.text: we charge a $25 administration fee

items.question: What deductible applies to emergency medical travel claims?
items.reference_answer: $100 for each unrelated incident or claim.

evidence.text: A deductible of $ 100 is applied to each unrelated incident or claim

items.question: How long do I have to submit a travel claim?
items.reference_answer: Within 6 months from the date the incident happened.

evidence.text: all claims must be submitted within 6 months from the date the incident happened

items.question: How much is paid for meals and accommodation if my return home from a trip is delayed by illness?
items.reference_answer: Up to $150 per day, to a maximum of $1,500 per policy, with a physician's or nurse practitioner's written statement and original receipts.

evidence.text: We'll pay up to $150 per day, to a maximum of $1,500 per policy

items.question: Up to what age is emergency medical travel coverage available?
items.reference_answer: It is only available to those under age 70; coverage expires on the insured's 70th birthday.

evidence.text: is only available to those under age 70

items.question: What is the lifetime maximum for homecare, private nursing, medical equipment and prosthetic appliances under the catastrophic coverage benefit?

evidence.text: There is a lifetime maximum of $100,000 for homecare

items.question: Which prescription drugs are covered, and which are excluded?
items.reference_answer: Covered: generic drugs and medicines listed in Manulife's formulary at the time of the claim (Quebec residents: the formulary or the RAMQ list), prescribed by a physician, nurse practitioner or dentist and dispensed by a licensed pharmacist. Excluded include preventive vaccines, anti-obesity drugs, vitamins and supplements, over-the-counter drugs, erectile dysfunction drugs, smoking cessation aids, drugs paid by a government plan and more than a three-month supply without approval.

evidence.text: We'll only reimburse charges for generic drugs and medicines that are listed in the applicable Manulife formulary

items.question: Is dental covered on the DrugPlus plan, and how are dental fees capped?
items.reference_answer: No, the dental benefit is not available on DrugPlus. Where dental is covered, charges are reimbursed up to the Provincial Dental Association Suggested Fee Guide for General Practitioners in effect when the services are done.

evidence.text: Dental Association Suggested Fee Guide for General Practitioners

items.question: What is the travel deductible, and what happens if I don't contact the Assistance Centre within 24 hours of being hospitalized?
items.reference_answer: The deductible is $100 per unrelated incident or claim. If you don't contact the Assistance Centre within the first 24 hours of hospitalization, the benefit is limited to 70% of eligible expenses up to $25,000, unless you or your travelling companion were unable to call because of an incapacitating illness or injury.

evidence.text: 70% of eligible expenses to a maximum of $25,000

items.question: Which paramedical practitioners are covered while travelling, and what is the maximum?
items.reference_answer: Licensed or registered physiotherapists, chiropractors, chiropodists, podiatrists and osteopaths (including x-rays) when required for emergency treatment, up to $300.

evidence.text: Charges up to $300 for services provided by a licensed or registered: physiotherapist, chiropractor

items.question: How soon must I report an accidental dental injury, and when must treatment start and finish?
items.reference_answer: Notify Manulife within 90 days of the accident; treatment must begin within 90 days and end within 1 year from the date of the accident (and approval is needed before treatment, except emergency pain relief).

evidence.text: ensure the treatment begins within 90 days and ends within 1 year from the date of the accident

items.question: Under the catastrophic coverage benefit, what is the annual threshold and the annual maximum for homecare and medical equipment expenses?
items.reference_answer: After an annual threshold of $7,500 in these expenses, coverage is 100% up to $25,000 per anniversary year (with a $100,000 lifetime maximum).

evidence.text: up to a maximum of $25,000 per anniversary year, after you reach an annual threshold of $7,500

items.question: How do I submit a claim?
items.reference_answer: Claims are paid for eligible expenses from the last 12 months, by direct deposit or cheque within 60 days. Submissions go online through manulife.ca/secureserve or by mail, with the approval notice and vendor invoice where prior authorization applies. For travel claims, call 1-800-805-1008 for a Claim Authorization and Release Form and submit it with original detailed invoices or receipts within 6 months of the incident.

evidence.text: We'll pay for eligible expenses by direct deposit or cheque to the policy owner or a service provider within 60 days
call 1 -800-805-1008 to request a Claim Authorization and Release Form

items.question: How does the catastrophic coverage benefit relate to the regular prescription drug benefit?
items.reference_answer: The regular drug benefit reimburses generic formulary drugs up to the amounts in the Schedule of Benefits. The catastrophic benefit (not available in Quebec) pays 100% of formulary prescription drug costs after out-of-pocket drug expenses reach the threshold in the Schedule of Benefits for the anniversary year.

evidence.text: Prescription drug benefit
This benefit provides 100% coverage for prescription drugs after a threshold of prescription drug costs

items.question: Who counts as a dependent child, and what happens to their coverage when they no longer qualify?
items.reference_answer: A dependent is a child on the application you're legally responsible for, under 21, unmarried, not working full-time and relying on you for support. A child who turns 21, marries, becomes an orphan or gets full-time employment must be removed, and can convert to their own policy by contacting Manulife within 30 days.

evidence.text: An insured child is under 21 years old, unmarried, doesn't work full -time, and relies on you for financial support
they may continue their own coverage under a separate policy

items.question: How is ambulance transportation covered at home compared with while travelling?
items.reference_answer: At home: medically necessary ground and air emergency ambulance to a hospital within your province, the difference above the government allowance, with no lifetime maximum. While travelling: licensed ground ambulance to the nearest qualified facility, and air ambulance to the nearest appropriate facility or a Canadian hospital when pre-approved and arranged by the Assistance Centre.

evidence.text: There is no lifetime maximum
The cost of air ambulance to the nearest appropriate medical facility or to a Canadian hospital when approved by us

items.question: Is physiotherapy covered both at home and while travelling?
items.reference_answer: Yes. At home, physiotherapy is covered under paramedical services. While travelling, physiotherapists are covered up to $300 when required for emergency treatment. The catastrophic benefit also covers physiotherapy 100% for one benefit year after an accident requiring at least a 24-hour hospital stay.

evidence.text: Paramedical services
Charges up to $300 for services provided by a licensed or registered: physiotherapist

items.question: What does the policy say about pregnancy-related coverage?
items.reference_answer: Preferred hospital accommodation covers up to 2 days of pregnancy-related hospitalization if you were less than 21 weeks pregnant on the application date (not recognized at 21 weeks or more). Emergency travel benefits exclude childbirth and complications after the 26th week of pregnancy.

evidence.text: If you're less than 21 weeks pregnant on the application date, we'll cover a maximum of 2 days of h ospitalization
after the 26th week of pregnancy
